doc.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023

title: Childhood record player, toy soldiers and the 1812 Overture
summary: Malone recalls playing war with his brother in Hawaii to 1812 Overture and getting his own violin at five.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: This has really been a fascinating conversation, I think we could probably do a part 2 and a part 3.
Yeah. Well maybe we should but I want to close with a question about — I read about the plastic military figures and “1812 Overture.” Is that ringing a bell?
Yes well it says in your own hand, or in an interview, that when you were a little kid your parents bought your first record player.

Yes, yes. I was living in Hawaii at the time, I was four or five years old and I heard all this music and yeah, we used to play war. My dad was a military officer. We used to play war. My brother and I used to play war and my brother got a violin and, you know, because of listening to that music, you know the violin [scats] I can still remember all that music, and so my brother got a violin and the only reason I wanted a violin is because, hey, my brother’s got one I want one too. You know that’s what childhood — so I got my own violin. I guess he got one when he was six — he was two years older than me. So by the time he was seven I was five, and my parents bought me a violin and I still
have it. It’s a 1/16. It almost looks like a toy violin or something. I’m going to get it re- strung and fixed up, put it on the wall.
Nice, well it said something about toy soldiers — you’d play war with the toy soldiers.
Yes. It had those little miniature — I’m trying to — was it a Mattel? I’m trying to remember, little toy soldiers and we used play with, my brother and I used to play with them on the floor.
While we were playing that music. Yeah. And it was indeed about war. That music was about war.
Yeah. Like the trumpet stuff and lots of minor key stuff. And you know some orchestras even today if they do an outdoor concert they’ll bring the cannons, yeah, for the finale part.
